<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-dev-docs.mjs from openvireo-sdk develop@86e6cd2; do not edit by hand. -->

Every error the SDK throws on purpose is an `OpenVireoError` with a machine-readable `code`. Errors from a
server also carry the HTTP `status`, and are `HttpError`s with the response `body` and `retryAfter` (seconds,
from `Retry-After`). Messages are for people and may change; branch on `code`.

```ts {linenos=false}
import { isOpenVireoError, isUnreachable } from "@openvireo/sdk";

try {
  await account.login({ email, password });
} catch (e) {
  if (isOpenVireoError(e, "invalid_secret_key")) {
    await account.login({ email, password, secretKey: await askForSecretKey() });
  } else if (isUnreachable(e)) {
    // no network, or a gateway answered 502/503/504: try again later
  } else {
    throw e;
  }
}
```

`isUnreachable(e)` is true for `network_error` and for `502`, `503` and `504`: the server couldn't be reached,
as opposed to refusing the request.

### Signing in and sessions {#signing-in-and-sessions}

| Code | Status | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|---|
| `unauthorized` | 401 | Wrong email or password, a Secret Key that doesn't match, or a session that is no longer valid | Ask again, or sign in again |
| `invalid_secret_key` | | The Secret Key is malformed, or this device has none for the account | Ask for the Secret Key (Emergency Kit) |
| `mfa_required` | | The account has two-factor authentication and no code was given | Pass `totp` |
| `invalid_mfa` | 401 | Wrong two-factor code | With a `totp` function, `login` asks again by itself |
| `mfa_expired` | 401/410 | The sign-in timed out or the code was wrong too often | Start the sign-in again |
| `session_expired` | 410 | The session, or a link such as a recovery link, expired or was used | Sign in again |
| `token_reused` | 401 | A refresh token was used twice, a sign it was copied; the server ends the session | Sign in again; `onSignedOut` reports it |
| `signed_out` | | The call needs a signed-in account | Sign in first |
| `weak_kdf` | | The account's password hashing settings are below the minimum the client accepts | Report it; don't continue |
| `opaque_failed` | | The OPAQUE module couldn't load or a protocol step failed | Check that the WASM module is bundled |

### Account recovery {#account-recovery}

See [Account recovery](/docs/sdk/recovery/#errors) for `recovery_not_ready`, `recovery_cancelled`,
`restore_locked` and `invalid_proof`.

### Vaults and sync {#vaults-and-sync}

| Code | Status | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|---|
| `forbidden` | 403 | The account or service account doesn't have the role this needs (e.g. `write` for a change) | Ask a vault manager for access |
| `not_found` | 404 | No such vault, entry, member, … | |
| `not_available_offline` | | Offline, and this vault was never synced on this device | Go online once |
| `vault_key_mismatch` | | None of the keys or passwords opens the server copy | Self-hosted: ask for the database's new password. Accounts: the keys are out of date; reload the vault list |
| `no_vault_key` | | The account holds no usable key for this vault | Reload the vault list; ask a manager to share it again |
| `too_many_conflicts` | 412 | The vault kept changing during the sync, five times in a row. Local changes are kept | Sync again |
| `server_rolled_back` | | The server returned an older copy than this device already synced: restored from a backup, or tampered with | Ask the user; `syncKdbx` with `acceptServerState: true` merges anyway |
| `server_lost_database` | | The server no longer has a database this device synced before | Ask the user before uploading it again |
| `vault_upload_failed` | | `importVault` created the vault, but the first upload failed (`VaultUploadError`, with `.vault`) | `e.vault.sync()` later |
| `kdbx_error` | | The file couldn't be read or written as KDBX, or the vault isn't open | |
| `merge_failed` | | The merge couldn't combine the two copies | Report it, with the databases if possible |

### References and entries {#references-and-entries}

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `invalid_reference` | Not a valid `ov://` reference (empty segment, bad percent-encoding, missing field) |
| `entry_not_found` | No entry, or several, match the reference; use the entry UUID when titles repeat |
| `conflict` (409) | `create: "only"` and the entry exists; on the server, also an email that is taken or a key version that moved on |

### HTTP and transport {#http-and-transport}

Server errors keep the server's `code`; without one, the status decides:

| Status | Code |
|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` |
| 401 | `unauthorized` |
| 403 | `forbidden` |
| 404 | `not_found` |
| 409 | `conflict` |
| 410 | `gone` |
| 412 | `precondition_failed` |
| 428 | `precondition_required` |
| 429 | `rate_limited` (see `retryAfter`) |
| 5xx | `server_error` |

`network_error` means the request never got an answer, and `aborted` that your `AbortSignal` cancelled it.

### Crypto {#crypto}

`decryption_failed`, `unsupported_version`, `invalid_public_keys`, `invalid_token` and `low_order_point` mean
data didn't decrypt or verify: wrong key, corrupted data, a malformed token, or keys whose signature doesn't
match. They shouldn't happen in normal use. Don't retry them; report them.
